page: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-2GB is an entry-tier virtual server instance powered by AMD EPYC 9575F processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture on a KVM hypervisor. The configuration includes 2 shared vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supported by 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 64 KB of L1 instruction/data cache. The system is provisioned with 2.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1.0 GB per core ratio, along with 50 GB of local SSD storage and a single complimentary public IPv4 address. It does not include dedicated graphics acceleration hardware.

Performance benchmarks show pronounced strengths in single-threaded compute tasks alongside predictable entry-level memory limitations. In stress-ng single-core execution, the instance ranks in the top tier, bolstered by hardware-accelerated instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and SHA-NI. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression similarly register top-tier throughput. Conversely, multi-threaded operations reflect the modest core count, with stress-ng multi-core and static web serving throughput performing at median benchmark levels, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark database operations register lower performance brackets due to the 2.0 GB memory ceiling.

From an infrastructure and cost efficiency perspective, this instance maximizes single-thread processing efficiency without the overhead of oversized memory allocations. The primary engineering tradeoff is the shared CPU model combined with limited RAM, which precludes large in-memory databases or multi-threaded compilations. The server is functionally suitable for lightweight web serving, reverse proxying, microservices, background job workers, and low-footprint cache layers.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-2GB is a shared virtual server configuration built on the AMD EPYC 9575F processor running on the KVM hypervisor. The instance provides 2 x86_64 vCPUs across 2 physical cores clocked at 2.0 GHz, bundled with 2.0 GB of memory and 50 GB of local SSD storage, without GPU acceleration. CPU feature flags include AVX-512 extensions and hardware cryptography acceleration. Benchmark evaluations show exceptional single-core processing capability, scoring in the top 10 percent for stress-ng single-core tests as well as single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations. However, memory subsystem benchmarks and multi-threaded decompression indicate constrained throughput, reflecting the low 1.0 GB per core memory allocation and shared execution model. Storage performance supports steady static web serving throughput alongside moderate Redis throughput. This hardware profile provides cost-effective compute capacity for entry-level microservices, lightweight web serving, small proxy routers, and background task processing where heavy memory capacity is unnecessary.
